entries.appliesTo: administration of each institution under the Campus Accountability and Safety Act (postsecondary campuses)

sources.trainingRequired: § 3399.16(A)-(B)(1) — 'the administration of each institution, in consultation with campus or local law enforcement agencies, shall develop and distribute, not less than four times per academic year through in-person or online delivery or both, information to students regarding power-based violence' … 'Instruction on … the identification, prevention, dangers, and prohibition of power-based violence and how to detect potential threats to school safety exhibited online, including on any social media platform.'

flags: AI content is definitional only: § 3399.12(5)(b) adds to 'power-based violence' — 'Any conduct prohibited by R.S. 14:73.13 or 73.14, or any successor statute, involving media generated by artificial intelligence or deepfake media depicting sexual imagery.' No AI-specific compliance duty is imposed; the criminal prohibitions live in cross-referenced statutes not in this text (rule 4).

Family fit is lossy: bill binds postsecondary institutions ('each institution' under the Campus Accountability and Safety Act, R.S. 17:3399.12 et seq.), but the only education family in the v1.0 vocabulary is education-k12; no higher-ed family exists.

trainingRequired coding is lossy: the duty is periodic distribution of safety-education information ('not less than four times per academic year'), including at new student orientation and posted on the institution's website (§ 3399.16(C)(1)), rather than a formal training program.

Minor-student provision: § 3399.16(C)(2) — 'If the student receiving the information required by Subsections B and C of this Section is a minor, the information shall also be provided to his parent or legal guardian.' No matching param in the education-k12 vocabulary.
No penalty or enforcement provision in this text; exposure omitted (silence is silence).
